preamble: In Goidelic, word-initial Proto-Celtic *w became /f/, whereas Brythonic changed it to gw-. Ogham inscriptions still write the glide (Primitive Irish VENDOGNI, *viras), and Old Irish has f: *wiros 'man' > fer (Welsh gŵr), *wīros 'true' > fír (Welsh gwir), *windos 'white' > find (Welsh gwyn). Early Latin loans whose v was still [w] took part (vīnum > fín). The result survives in Irish, Scottish Gaelic and Manx. No comparable case outside Celtic has been verified.

examples.to: fer; Irish and Scottish Gaelic fear, Manx fer
examples.note: Brythonic has gw- from the same etymon: Welsh gŵr.

examples.to: fír; Irish fíor, Scottish Gaelic fìor, Manx feer
find; Irish and Scottish Gaelic fionn, Manx fynn
fín; Irish fíon, Scottish Gaelic fìon
